problem: Which EEG-to-BOLD estimates could support one clinical action? Test regional fidelity and failure modes before considering patient-specific fMRI replacement.
aim:
Thesis aim: identify which BOLD information is recoverable, then build models that generalise and know when to abstain. This explores a possible computer science PhD.

Candidate contributions: multimodal system identification; robust person/site transfer; calibrated, selective regional prediction. Establish novelty against UnEBOLT, MARBLE and UniEFS, rather than promising clinical replacement.

First application: a wakefulness advisory prompting technologist review. Compare direct arousal prediction: BOLD synthesis must earn its complexity. One regional feedback target is a conditional second route. Diagnostic mapping needs a separate validation programme.
hypothesis: Predictive value may depend more on measured information and target definition than on model size. Cross people, duration, sensors and capacity on fixed holdouts. A nonlinear gain would favour richer models; an added-sensor gain would favour acquisition. Null results and small learning curves cannot establish a biological ceiling.
models:
UnEBOLT [1] | 64 regions, r .418.
Proposed: one regional feedback target.

UniEFS [2] | 512 regions, r .367.
EEG-only Parkinson classification probe;
patient BOLD unvalidated.

MARBLE [3] | 64 regions, r .434; 2.6M parameters.
Proposed: compact regional prediction.
methods: ds006040 development: 27 people/54 runs; three outer folds, 96 fitted outer cells. Inner tuning separate. Matched inputs: 300 EEG-power features, ECG timing/availability or both; ridge/small MLP. Cross 4/12 training people x 120/240 retained target-seconds. One seed; four equal-weight MLP target groups. Published models were not reproduced.
work_packages: Rank montage, history and sensors; test held-out gains against cost-matched choices.
Learn shared dynamics with counted calibration. Test regional gains beyond ridge and state/physiology controls.
Report error at useful coverage under stated shift assumptions; compare quality rejection.
clinical_gate:
Clinical precedent: Prism's fMRI-informed EEG biofeedback is cleared for adjunctive PTSD treatment; diagnostic interpretation is excluded [4].
Proposed: wakefulness support or one regional feedback target. Disease classification does not verify patient BOLD recovery.
M3 limits: inherited preprocessing is retrospective; no absolute %BOLD calibration. Causal inputs do not establish end-to-end live use. Sparse ECG; one development site/seed; clinical benefit untested [5].
